subtitle: Modal verbs for how sure you are, and criticism after the fact
words.intro: Sunday, 8:15 p.m. Half of Germany knows who did it by 8:40. They say so in careful stages: he might have, he must have, he can’t have. It is the best grammar drill on television.

grammar[0].fact: The scale runs: *muss* (nearly certain), *dürfte* (probably), *könnte* (possibly), *kann nicht* (impossible). English muddles these, so *he must be* often comes out too strongly in German, and you end up accusing someone you only meant to suspect.

grammar[1].fact: German meetings love this form, since it blames nobody at all. *Das hätte vermieden werden können* has a whole committee in it. At home, *Du hättest anrufen können* is quite enough, and you won’t need the passive.

listen.intro: A radio play, read aloud. At each scene break, say who it might be, who it must be, and who it can’t be.
speak.intro: How sure are you? Short claims with the tutor, each hedged to the degree you actually believe it.

opener.caption: Nachts in Münster: Hier wird gerade ein Krimi gedreht, und alle tun, als wäre etwas passiert.
document.intro: A real wanted notice from a newspaper of 1818, in Fraktur. A machine builder has run off with his employer’s carriage. Look for *angeblich*, which you met in this book. Two hundred years later, it does exactly the same job.
document.fact: Notices like this one were a newspaper’s own crime series. This one gives his height, his hair and even his coat, down to the English cut. Whether they ever caught Ernst Neubauer, this page doesn’t say.
document.tasks[1].instruction: Say each with soll or dürfte.
reading.intro: Sunday evening at Lena’s. The crime show is on, as it is every Sunday. Nobody is allowed to speak, and everybody is speaking. Max has seen only the first ten minutes. Frau Huber has come with her own armchair cushion, and she has never once been wrong.
reading.photos[0].caption: Polizeiabsperrung: Hier muss etwas passiert sein.
reading.fact: Germans call watching a big match or crime show together *Public Viewing*, an English-looking phrase that means something quite different in English. Each city has its team, and the show has been running since 1970. Many bars put it on the big screen, and woe betide anyone who talks.
reading.tasks[1].instruction: Say each with the right modal.
